verses.1: He said that this was a metaphor for them: they should always pray to Him and not resist.
verses.2: He said: “The judge was someone who lived in a city where people did not fear the gods, nor did they try to harm others.”
verses.3: There was also a woman in that city who came to him and said, “He has denied me from my opponent.”
verses.4: And he didn’t want to do it for a long time. But after that, he said to himself, “Even if I don’t fear the gods, I still won’t obey any human commands.”
verses.5: Therefore, I will repay her by giving her this comfort. This way, she won’t be left alone in a state of despair.
verses.6: But the Lord said, “Have you heard what the judge says about injustice?”
verses.7: But the God will not carry out the punishment that he has chosen for those who have been chosen by him to serve him, day and night. He will be patient with them.
verses.8: I say to you that they will be punished promptly. But will the son of man come and find out what is true on earth?
verses.9: He also said to those who believed in him that they were indeed just and capable of ruling over the rest. This was a mockery, after all.
verses.10: Two people went up to the temple to pray. One of them was a Pharisee, and the other was a commoner.
verses.11: The Pharisee was constantly thinking these things to himself. “God, thank you that I am not like other people. You do not steal, are unjust, or commit adultery. You are indeed a just God.”
verses.12: I observe the Sabbath day; I give thanks for everything I own.
verses.13: But that beauteous figure, who was standing far away, did not even want to raise his eyes towards the sky. Instead, he remained silent, saying, “Oh God, have mercy on this sinner.”
verses.14: I say to you, he who is humble will be brought down to his own level in relation to his master’s house. For everyone who elevates himself will be humbled, while those who are humble will be elevated.
verses.15: He also brought them the infants, so that they could be breastfed by them. When the disciples saw this, they praised him for it.
verses.16: But Jesus called them and said, “Come to me, children. Do not be afraid. For of such is the kingdom of God.”
verses.17: I say to you, whoever does not submit his kingdom to God like a child, shall not enter it.
verses.18: And someone asked the leader, saying, “Good teacher, what shall I do in order to receive eternal life as a legacy?”
verses.19: Then Jesus said to him, “What do you call me good? No one can be called good unless they are God.”
verses.20: You know the commands. Do not commit adultery, do not kill, do not steal, do not lie. Respect your father and your mother.
verses.21: And he said, “All of this I have planned from a young age.”
verses.22: And when Jesus heard this, he said to him, “There is still one thing you need to do. Sell all that you have and give it to the poor. Then you will have treasure in heaven. And follow me.”
verses.23: And when he heard these words, he became overjoyed, for he was indeed very rich.
verses.24: When Jesus saw this, he said, “How difficult it is for those who possess money to enter the kingdom of God.”
verses.25: For it is better to enter through poverty, rather than to become rich and enter the kingdom of God.
verses.26: And those who heard said, “Who can possibly survive?”
verses.27: And he said, “What is impossible for humans, is possible for God.”
verses.28: And Peter said, “Look, we have followed you, even though we have lost our own sight.”
verses.29: And he said to them, “I tell you that no one can leave his home, or his wife, or brothers, or parents, or children, because of the kingdom of God.”
verses.30: He who does not receive an eternal life in this time and in the coming days.
verses.31: After taking those twelve people with him, he said to them, “Look, we are going to Jerusalem. Then all that has been written by the prophets will be fulfilled for the Son of Man.”
verses.32: For it will be given over to the nations, and they will be troubled and upset by it.
verses.33: And when they strike him, they kill him. On the third day, he will rise again.
verses.34: And they did not do any of these things either. The meaning of this was hidden from them, and they did not understand what was said.
verses.35: And during his journey to Jerusalem, a blind man sat down along the road, asking for help.
verses.36: And when he heard the crowd arguing about what this meant, he was confused.
verses.37: They told him that Jesus of Nazareth had arrived.
verses.38: And he said, “Jesus son of David, have mercy on me.”
verses.39: And those who led the way tried to get him to be quiet. But he refused to do so. Son of David, please have mercy on me.
verses.40: But Jesus constantly commanded him to come to Him. When he arrived, Jesus asked him a question.
verses.41: What do you want me to do? He said, “Lord, so that I may look back.”
verses.42: And Jesus said to him, “Look! Your faith has saved you.”
verses.43: And he also paid attention to it, and followed it, praising the God along with it. And everyone in the crowd, seeing this, offered worship to the God.
